prior_exposure: v0.4 counts and 33 narrative reviews exposed; v0.5 ontology joins and alert counts not computed
population: Fixed 4,419 v0.4 programs and 98 candidate links. No new origin members or clinical labels. Mapping coverage is conditional on this selected subset.
normalization: Unicode NFKC, casefold, whitespace only. Do not remove punctuation, numbers, stage, genotype or negation.

equivalence.ambiguity: All candidate IDs retained. No label precedence or favorable tie break. Unmapped and ambiguous terms remain unresolved.

prior_risk.sources: All experimental-product possible rows from the sealed origin index for the same exact drug ID
prior_risk.known_start: ACTUAL original precision upper bound at/before origin; preserve missing/estimated dates and mixed phase as uncertainty
prior_risk.higher_phase: Numerical stage above baseline, or mixed phase whose highest declared stage exceeds baseline
prior_risk.interpretation: Same-ID higher phase is a prior-risk alert; hierarchy-related terms never establish equivalence. Regimen/population equivalence is not assumed. Original origin membership/labels unchanged.

clinical_scope.behavior: Exact non-disease terms are outside the disease-focused sensitivity view, not biological failures. Broad terms require scope review, never automatic family merge.
context_fields: study title as separately tagged study-wide context
unknowns: arm activation and experimental first dosing
clinical_scope.context_comparison: Report positive text signals and their source fields. Missing signal is unknown. A difference is an alert, not proof of incompatible populations; matching words never establish equivalence.

outputs: condition map sealed before outcome context joins
no_event_reenumeration: This stage audits fixed v0.4 membership/links. It is not a newly enumerated ontology-normalized clinical cohort or a recall estimate.
validation: Synthetic relation/ambiguity/negation/context tests; parent/raw/receipt hashes; original frame row proofs; full existing regressions; no scientific gold claim.

primary_sources.supports: Open Targets covers diseases, phenotypes, biological processes and measurements; ontology mapping alone is not a clinical-disease filter.
Disease products distinguish synonym relations and hierarchy. Pinned local schema checked directly; web page requires JavaScript.
